title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 6th District
area: Middle and Upper Middle Tennessee, under the congressional map Tennessee redrew in May 2026. Incumbent Rep. John Rose did not seek re-election to this seat.

context.text: Tennessee redrew its congressional district boundaries in May 2026 (mid-decade redistricting); the filing deadline for U.S. House seats was reopened until May 15, 2026 after the new map was signed into law.
Incumbent Rep. John Rose (R) is not on the ballot for this seat; Ballotpedia's candidate list for the district shows no incumbent running in the 2026 general election.

Johnny Garrett, a state representative, won the Republican primary in a four-candidate field, defeating Van Hilleary, a former U.S. representative (TN-4, 1995–2003) and former chief of staff to U.S. Rep. John Rose, 43.4% to 29.9%.
Mike Croley won the Democratic primary with 29.0% of the vote in a five-candidate field.

candidates.name: Mike Croley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Democratic primary with 29.0% of the vote in a five-candidate field

priorities.text: Says he is running because he watched the federal government "get gutted by billionaires and cowards" and wants to fight for working families, teachers, and veterans.
priorities.quote: I watched the government I worked for get gutted by billionaires and cowards. I'm not a polished politician, I'm a problem solver.

priorities.text: Campaign platform: protect the environment, legalize marijuana, raise teacher pay, and invest in rural infrastructure.
Says he will fight for fair wages and access to healthcare.

positions.summary: His campaign FAQ says he believes in ending broad tariffs.
positions.quote: Mike believes in ending broad tariffs

positions.summary: In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he said ending tax loopholes and more evenly taxing the ultra wealthy is a priority.
positions.quote: Ending tax loopholes and restructuring our tax structure to more evenly tax the ultra wealthy is a priority for me.

positions.summary: In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he listed raising the federal minimum wage to $20 per hour.
positions.quote: Raising the federal minimum wage to $20 per hour.

positions.summary: In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he said the federal government should spend much more on health care benefits and that he supports universal basic healthcare.
positions.quote: Much more, I fully support universal basic healthcare.

positions.summary: In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he said he does not support a federal ban on abortion.
positions.quote: It is absurd that one person feels they can tell another person what they can and cannot do with their own bodies.

positions.summary: In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he said enforcement under the second Trump term has been too strict and that ICE needs an overhaul that may mean abolishing the current agency.
positions.quote: ICE needs a complete overhaul to the point that it is likely better to abolish the current agency and establish a new, more heavily regulated and mission-defined agency.

positions.summary: In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he said a president needs congressional approval to wage a war.
In a Nashville Banner questionnaire he listed making Tennessee the leader in green, renewable energy among his policies.
positions.quote: making Tennessee the leader in green, renewable energy

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026) and campaign FAQ. Reporting that he opposes U.S. military aid to Israel and supports "safeguards around gun ownership" came from a reporter's summary, not his own words, so no israel_aid or guns position was recorded.

candidates.name: Johnny Garrett
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Republican primary, defeating Van Hilleary, 43.4% to 29.9%

priorities.text: Said he supports President Trump's agenda: "I'll stand with President Trump to finish the wall, deport all illegal immigrants, cut our taxes, and stop China from buying up our land."
priorities.quote: I'll stand with President Trump to finish the wall, deport all illegal immigrants, cut our taxes, and stop China from buying up our land.

priorities.text: Ran on his state legislative record, saying he "banned biological men from women's sports, combatted illegal immigration, and defended the unborn and led the charge to back law enforcement."
priorities.quote: I've already taken on the woke left in Nashville and won as your state representative; banned biological men from women's sports, combatted illegal immigration, and defended the unborn and led the charge to back law enforcement, our first responders, and balance our budget.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he implemented a Tennessee State Border Czar to work with ICE to deport all illegal immigrants from the state, and supports finishing the border wall.
positions.quote: Johnny took action in the Tennessee House to implement a State Border Czar who will work hand in glove with ICE to deport all illegal aliens from the Volunteer State.

positions.summary: His campaign site says that as a Tennessee state representative he passed legislation restricting competition in women's sports by sex and pledges to continue that effort in Washington.
positions.quote: As State Representative, Johnny passed legislation banning men from competing in women’s sports

record.text: As a Tennessee state representative, says he helped pass legislation restricting transgender participation in women's school sports.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site states positions on Israel ("every available resource to defend itself"), Second Amendment (general), and "100% Pro-Life" (no legal-access policy stated); these were not recorded as positions under the brief's rules. He did not answer the Nashville Banner questionnaire.

candidates.name: Christopher Monday

priorities.text: Says his campaign focuses on defending individual liberties and taking the oath of office seriously.

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he said tariffs drive prices up and should end.
positions.quote: For one end the tariff wars which drive prices up for everything

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he said the executive branch must receive approval from Congress before going to war.
positions.quote: Yes, again according to Article I of the Constitution the Executive Branch must receive approval from the Legislature before going to war.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his July 2026 Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire. His campaign site (CMondayForLiberty.com, per the Banner) returned an access error and could not be read.

statements.quote: I believe it’s a state level issue, not federal.
statements.context: In the Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), answering whether he supports a federal ban on abortion

statements.quote: ICE has abused its authority and has repeatedly ignored the law by refusing to acknowledge the rights of the people they detained.
statements.context: In the Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), on immigration enforcement in the second Trump term

statements.quote: The federal government should promote of an open and free market healthcare system.
statements.context: In the Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), on federal spending on health care benefits

statements.quote: That is more of a local and state issue, but I would push for lower taxes so people would be able to keep their money and afford housing.
statements.context: In the Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), on how he would address housing supply

candidates.name: Angus Purdy

priorities.text: Lists supporting rural hospitals, workers’ rights, public education, feeding families and protecting Social Security as his priorities.
priorities.quote: My priorities lie in supporting rural hospitals, workers’ rights, public education, feeding families, protecting social security

priorities.text: Says his campaign takes no donations from corporations or special interest groups.
priorities.quote: Our campaign refuses to take any donations from corporations or special interest groups.

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he said the ultra-wealthy should pay higher tax rates.
positions.quote: We need to return to tax rates that force the ultra-wealthy to pay their fair share.

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he said a president needs congressional approval to wage war and that declarations of war should be in the hands of Congress.
positions.quote: It is long past time to limit executive privilege and put declarations of war and military spending back in the hands of Congress.

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he said he supports nationwide rent control and a right to counsel for tenants.
positions.quote: We need nationwide universal rent control, and we must guarantee right to counsel for all tenants.

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he said he supports guaranteed universal health care and more federal spending.
positions.quote: I support guaranteed universal healthcare at no cost for all.

positions.summary: In the Nashville Banner questionnaire he called immigration enforcement too strict and said he wants ICE abolished.
positions.quote: I want to see ICE completely abolished and demand that every individual who served in the department be held liable for any violation of individual liberties.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his July 2026 Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire and campaign website. His answer on military aid referred to 'nations engaged in genocide' and was not recorded as an israel_aid position.

statements.context: In the Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), answering whether he supports a federal ban on abortion

statements.quote: We need a new aggressive approach by building publicly-owned social housing.
statements.context: In the Nashville Banner candidate questionnaire (July 2026), on how he would address housing supply
